title: Clinical outcome and implant survival after knee TEP change with the use of bone replacing implants
summary:
The implantation of the total knee arthroplasty (KTEP) is an established and successful procedure worldwide for knee arthrosis with exhausted conservative therapeutic measures. Bone loss, which already exists and arises from the replacement operation itself, is of particular relevance when changing a total knee endoprosthesis (KTEP).
There are bone-replacing implants that are used in different places and are sometimes connected to the implant. The name differs according to this and also according to the defect size ("Sleeves", "Cones" and "Wedges"). In this study, patients who have had bone-replacing implants implanted during a total knee replacement operation should be asked about implant survival and the revision rate. Furthermore, patient satisfaction and the subjective function of the joint are to be examined as part of the patient survey using questionnaires. In addition, the radiological recordings that have already been carried out are to be analyzed with regard to common radiological criteria for knee arthroplasty (loosening, joint and implant position).
conditions: Presence of a knee joint prosthesis

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Male or female patients in the age group ≥ 18 years 
- Performed surgery using cones, sleeves or wedges as bone-replacing implant systems
Exclusion criteria:
Renewed revision of the knee TEP with replacement of individual or all components
